title: Shipyard Welder
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk Zhou Lin（Zhou Lin, a shipyard welder in his thirties, buzz cut, weld scar on the cheekbone, scorched-brown fire suit and steel-toe boots, dark-green TIG welding helmet on the shoulder, rough hands dusted with iron filings） carries a dark-green welding helmet into the dry-dock welding shed（An iron-sheet welding shed on the dry dock's west side, explosion-proof lamps and fume hoods overhead, weld slag and grinding discs on the floor, ozone in the air） and strikes a test arc with the TIG welding torch（A deep-blue-handled TIG welding torch, tungsten tip bright, gas hose coiled, nozzle undamaged）.

A row of five brass-hood explosion-proof work lamps（A row of five brass-hood explosion-proof work lamps hung on iron hooks on the shed crossbeam, glass chimneys polished bright） hangs on the shed crossbeam; Zhou Lin wipes each glass chimney clean.

Two shift-change bronze bells（Two shift-change bronze bells hung under the shed eaves, bodies scarred by strikes, sounding two low notes at shift change） hang under the shed eaves; Zhou Lin taps them lightly and the dull notes echo.
Zhou Lin checks the TIG welding torch tungsten and gas-hose fitting, confirming no leak.
Through the shed opening Zhou Lin watches rust-red hull outlines in the basin.
The intact TIG welding torch rests on the welding bench, nozzle reflecting the explosion-proof lamps' warm light.
Zhou Lin sits by the slag bin and unscrews his canteen for a few sips.
A distant crane whistle sounds; Zhou Lin puts the helmet back on.
He lightly grinds the bevel to be welded with an angle grinder; sparks briefly fly.
Zhou Lin opens the blue weld inspection log（A blue hard-cover weld inspection log with thickness-gauge readouts clipped in, neat writing, clean cover） and notes the day's weld numbers in ballpoint.
He sketches the bevel angle in the inspection log and marks thickness readings.
Zhou Lin closes the weld inspection log and tucks it back into the second drawer of the tool cabinet.
Blue-white arc light from the TIG welding torch sweeps across his cheek.
He tears off a scrap of sandpaper and wipes iron powder from his gloves.

At the outfitting pier（An outfitting pier reaching into the basin, bollards on the concrete quay, crane boom sweeping past, rust-red hulls in the distance） in the morning Zhou Lin greets the moored rust-red barge Rust Harbor（A rust-red riveted barge named Rust Harbor, white-painted name on the gunwale, deck piled with angle steel and a gas-cylinder cage）.

Young Xingzi（Young Xingzi: a lean welding apprentice around fifteen, copper-button work badge on the chest, oversized canvas coveralls, eyes clear and stubborn） jumps from Rust Harbor onto the pier and loops the cable onto a concrete bollard.

Zhou Lin points to the three enamel electrode-spec tags（Three enamel electrode-spec tags hung on the gas-cylinder cage, labeled J422, J506, and stainless wire） on the gas-cylinder cage and teaches Xingzi to tell J422 from J506.
Xingzi squats at the pier edge and curiously touches the rivets on Rust Harbor's gunwale.
Zhou Lin explains to Xingzi that when the shipyard shift bells sound twice the arc must stop.
Xingzi looks back at intact Rust Harbor; the copper-button work badge sways lightly on his chest.
Tide slaps the shore; the two walk along the pier toward the dry-dock welding shed.

In the plate-yard narrow aisle（A narrow aisle between upright plate racks, steel walls on both sides, white-powder safety lines on the ground, heavy shadows） Alan（Young welder Alan whose face closely resembles Xingzi's, but wearing charcoal-black long welding gloves and a bright-red epaulette vest over coveralls, manner bold） in charcoal-black long welding gloves looks back from the upright-plate shadows.
Alan walks slowly along the white-powder safety line; the bright-red epaulette vest stands out.
He brushes past a material cart; charcoal gloves flash in the plate reflection.
Alan knocks the rack to confirm the plate pins are locked.
He passes a figure at the aisle end and walks toward the outfitting area.
On the outfitting pier Xingzi and Alan stand side by side: one with a copper-button work badge, one in charcoal welding gloves.
Xingzi hands Alan a knocked-off slag chunk; they meet eyes briefly.
Alan straightens Xingzi's oversized coverall collar, then turns his face away.
They walk opposite ways along the pier; figures cross in the crane's shadow.
A burst of grinding rises; only cables sway lightly on the pier.
On a night months later Zhou Lin alone keeps watch in the dry-dock welding shed.

He opens the weld inspection log（The same weld inspection log soaked through with hydraulic oil, cover sticky and curling, writing blurred into a blot）; the cover is already soaked with hydraulic oil, sticky and curling.
Zhou Lin wipes grease from the TIG welding torch body with a rag.
Through the shed opening he watches warning buoys in the pitch-black basin.
The TIG welding torch rests quiet on the welding bench, gas hose coiled.
A shift-change bronze bell is bumped half a note by night wind, then falls silent.
In spring flood season Zhou Lin day after day restrikes arcs and patch-welds in the shed.
On another rain night he wraps the fire suit tight and keeps watch by the TIG welding torch.
At high summer noon the shed iron sheet burns hot; he rotates cooling.
In autumn fog the explosion-proof lamps' light struggles through smoke and dust.
On New Year's Eve Zhou Lin alone fills the weld inspection record to the last page.
In early spring he recalibrates the thickness gauge and resumes shipyard patrols.
Before typhoon season Zhou Lin reinforces the gas-cylinder cage straps.
After Frost's Descent he adds a small bucket of dry sand in the shed corner for backup.
In another ship-survey season he taps section by section listening to weld echoes.
On a snow-night shutdown Zhou Lin leaves only one explosion-proof lamp and keeps watch until dawn.
Zhou Lin changes the grinding disc and dresses a newly arrived rib-plate bevel.
He checks the fume-hood filter and shakes out settled weld ash.
He lifts the intact TIG welding torch again and short-arc test-welds a bead.
Rivet-gun rhythm rises from the pier; he looks up to listen.
Zhou Lin drops spent electrode stubs into an iron bucket and closes the lid.
At noon break he smokes outside the shed, tapping ash into a tin can.
In the afternoon he returns to the welding bench and continues patch-welding the manhole coaming.
At sunset he shuts the gas valve and locks the tool cabinet.
At dawn Zhou Lin patrols the outfitting pier; Rust Harbor still lies in the shallow bay.
He crouches to check whether Rust Harbor's gunwale rivets have loosened.
On the gas-cylinder cage those three electrode-spec tags still hang in place.
A blue-gray tug Tide Sound（A blue-gray harbor tug named Tide Sound, broad flat hull, no rust-red riveted-barge name—not the same as Rust Harbor） crosses the basin—broad flat hull, not Rust Harbor.
Zhou Lin stands on the pier recording fender wear exposed after the ebb.
He recoils the cable and presses it beside Rust Harbor's deck edge.
A distant crane slowly swings; morning fog begins to thin.
At nightfall Zhou Lin returns to the dry-dock welding shed and opens the oil-soaked weld inspection log.
He matches old numbers and adds today's patrol results.
He briefly restrikes the TIG welding torch; light shows the inspection log's sticky cover.
He wipes spatter dots from the helmet lens.
Basin wind rises; the shed iron sheet rattles lightly.
Zhou Lin extinguishes half the row of explosion-proof lamps, leaving only the work-station one.
In a rainstorm a crane cable suddenly snaps; the dry-dock welding shed shudders hard.
Standing water floods the welding bench; explosion-proof lamps swing violently.

While Zhou Lin rushes to save gear the TIG welding torch（The same TIG welding torch with ceramic nozzle cracked and blackened, tungsten askew, gas hose greasy） ceramic nozzle cracks black and the tungsten skews.
In the basin Rust Harbor is swept by a runaway hook and jolts hard.
Another crack—Rust Harbor（Rust Harbor tips after a crane cable snaps, hull bottom-up half-sunk in dry-dock mud water, mast light out） tips; hull bottom-up half-sinks into mud water.
Zhou Lin rushes from the shed, clamping hard on the burned TIG welding torch.
Alarms blare; a safety whistle shatters into fragments in the rain.
Next day when rain eases Zhou Lin stands in the shed staring at the nozzle-burned TIG welding torch.
He traces the cracked ceramic nozzle with a finger, expression dark.
On a blank page of the weld inspection log he writes the date Rust Harbor was lost.
A berth diagram of Rust Harbor is still taped to the shed wall; Zhou Lin gazes at it a long time.
He takes one of the five explosion-proof work lamps from the crossbeam and sits alone in the faint light.
The burned TIG welding torch rests on the bench, gas hose hanging like a wounded snake.
A distant dredger rumbles; muddy spray rises in the basin.
Weeks later Zhou Lin brings tools and prepares to repair the TIG welding torch.

From a wooden crate he takes a spare torch head（A half-person-long spare torch head shaped much like the main torch, but with a black-rubber handle and no gas-hose fitting）—much like the main torch but with a black-rubber handle.
Zhou Lin removes the cracked nozzle and fits a new milky-white ceramic tip.

Tungsten re-sharpened, the TIG welding torch（The TIG welding torch fitted with a new milky-white ceramic nozzle, tungsten re-sharpened, gas hose wiped clean, ready to restrike an arc） is usable again; gas hose wiped clean.
He short-arc test-welds; the arc is steady and sharp again.
Zhou Lin puts the spare torch head back in the crate, no longer confused.

An orange-red mobile welding cart（A brand-new orange-red mobile welding cart with an inverter welder in the bed, white lettering 'Temporary Support'—utterly unlike Rust Harbor） rolls onto the outfitting pier—nothing like the already capsized Rust Harbor.

A yellow-vest white-hat shipyard safety officer（A lean shipyard safety officer, full beard, yellow reflective vest, white hard hat, build somewhat like Zhou Lin's, but with a safety-office badge on the shoulder） jumps onto the pier and talks beside Zhou Lin; the two look similar in build.
The safety officer points at the orange-red mobile welding cart and explains the temporary support grouping.
The welding cart horns and drives off; Zhou Lin alone watches from the pier.
He resets the safety cones and walks back to the shed along the bollards.

Into the plate-yard narrow aisle comes intern Xiaoman（New intern Xiaoman in a light-gray headscarf and brand-new coveralls, at a glance like young Xingzi, but with a sharper chin and shy eyes） in a light-gray headscarf—at a glance somewhat like young Xingzi.
Xiaoman tries tying a cable; Zhou Lin shakes his head—she is not Xingzi after all.
Xiaoman bows and withdraws; only upright-plate shadows remain in the aisle.

At dusk years later Zhou Lin（The same Zhou Lin: fire-suit cuff burned through, gauze on the left brow, walking slowly with a torch case as cane, gaze heavy but still locked on the weld）, cuff burned through and brow gauze on, leans on a torch case under the abandoned slipway（An old slipway ruin, rotten sleepers, water in the rail slots, a half keel support and a rusted gantry remaining）.
He looks up at the rusted gantry, gaze distant.
In the distance those two shift-change bronze bells under the shed eaves ring lightly in the wind; Zhou Lin stops to listen.
He presses a palm to a rotten sleeper as if saying goodbye.
Tide sounds far; slipway puddles mirror his figure.

By day adult Xingzi（Adult Xingzi: a welder in his twenties with broader shoulders, still wearing that copper-button work badge, fitted canvas coveralls, eyes steady） returns along the pier and hurries toward the abandoned slipway.
Under the slipway Xingzi reunites with injured Zhou Lin; they support each other.
By the shipyard-clinic iron bed Xingzi holds Zhou Lin's wasted hand.
Zhou Lin（Zhou Lin lies still with eyes closed on an iron bed in the shipyard clinic, face peaceful, breath gone）'s breath grows weak; at last he closes his eyes and passes away.
Outside the window the crane is still; basin wind falls quiet for an instant.
Behind the shed door Zhou Lin's scorched-brown fire suit still hangs; Xingzi reaches to stroke it gently.

By the brick pillar adult Xingzi stands before the newly nailed shipyard memorial brass plaque（A brass memorial plaque nailed to the welding-shed brick pillar, carved with 'Zhou Lin' and the hire year, edges already verdigris）.
Xingzi's fingertip traces Zhou Lin's name carved on the brass plaque.
He softly speaks the page number of the inspection record of Rust Harbor's loss, as if answering.
After the outfitting pier is dredged Xingzi writes the three characters of Rust Harbor on the empty berth and then erases them.
Passing the clinic corridor he sees Zhou Lin's old work badge in a glass cabinet.
Tide slaps the shore; Xingzi grips the copper-button work badge tight in his palm.

Alan（Alan after remaking his look still wears charcoal-black long welding gloves; the epaulette vest is now matte black, manner deeper） with his remade look arrives from the plate yard and briefly meets Xingzi's eyes under the abandoned slipway.
Xingzi and Alan stand side by side by the keel support: one quiet-eyed, one deep-mannered.
Alan still wears charcoal-black long welding gloves; Xingzi still wears the copper-button work badge.
They are silent a moment, then each turns and leaves the slipway.
The shot returns to years ago—that youth jumping from the barge onto the pier with a copper-button work badge appears again.
The opening moment returns—in the shed a deep-blue-handled torch strikes a test arc for the first time.
Flashback to the plate aisle—that charcoal-gloved figure in a bright-red epaulette vest slips past.
Again that row of five brass-hood explosion-proof lamps on the shed crossbeam appears.
Back to that pier of first meeting reaching into the basin, bollards and crane as before.
Xingzi opens again that oil-soaked weld inspection log and walks into the dry-dock welding shed.
By the gas-cylinder cage those three electrode-spec tags still hang.
Xingzi lifts the nozzle-replaced TIG welding torch; arc light fills the shed again.
He rolls the fire-suit cuffs tight and nods to confirm as Zhou Lin once did.
In basin dusk the new shift's shift-change bronze bells sound two light notes.
